subject: Social Habits
title: My friends
objectives: Children will play beside and with friends.
Children will say what a good friend does.
content: Playing with friends, being a good friend, and making friends.
teachingActivities: Notice and name friendly acts; let children choose play partners; help shy children join with a simple script such as "Can I play?"; avoid forcing friendships; use pairs and small groups; reassure children when a friend is absent.
learnerActivities: Play with a friend for a short time and say what a good friend does.
assessment: Observe whether each child plays with a friend for a short time and says one thing a good friend does.
expectedOutcomes: Plays with a friend for a short time.
Says one thing a good friend does.

lessons.title: Playing with friends
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play with a friend for a short time.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name family members and show love in simple ways.
lessons.starter: Sing "Friends, friends, I have friends. We play together, hand in hand."
teacherActivities: Show how two children can play with one ball.
Pair children and give them blocks.
learnerActivities: Child plays with a new friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how two children can play with one ball. Children: Children watch and wave.
Step 2. Teacher: Pair children and give them blocks. Children: Child plays beside a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Look, you are playing together." Children: Children smile at each other.
Step 4. Teacher: Change partners and play again. Children: Child plays with a new friend.

practical.title: Play with a friend
practical.safety: Use large toys with no small parts and supervise pairs closely. Step in gently if a child is left out.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and a friend.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose a friend and say their name.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Plays with a friend for a short time
lessons.homeConnection: Arrange short play with a friend and notice when they play well.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play with a friend for a short time" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Friends, friends, I have friends, we play together.

lessons.title: Being a good friend
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say what a good friend does.
successCriteria: Says one thing a good friend does
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name family members and show love in simple ways.
resources: Pictures of good friends sharing, helping, playing and comforting
lessons.starter: Show a puppet who shares and say "A good friend shares and plays nicely."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and say what the friend does.
Ask "What does a good friend do?"
Act out sharing, helping and comforting with a friend.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the action.
Child says or points to a picture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and say what the friend does. Children: Children look and say the action.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What does a good friend do?" Children: Child says or points to a picture.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out sharing, helping and comforting with a friend. Children: Child acts with a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "I am a good friend." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Friend actions
steps: Say I am a good friend.
practical.safety: Supervise acting closely so play stays gentle. Offer a wave or high five instead of touch if a child prefers.

differentiation.support: Act together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give an example of a good friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What does a good friend do?

expectedOutcomes: Says what a good friend does
lessons.conclusion: Sing the friendship song and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Praise your child when they are a good friend.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say what a good friend does" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making friends
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will practise asking to join a game.
successCriteria: Says "Can I play?" with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name family members and show love in simple ways.
lessons.starter: Use the puppet to say "Can I play with you?" and let the friend say yes.
teacherActivities: Show how to ask "Can I play?" and wait for the answer.
Say "If a friend says yes, play. If not, try another friend."
Let children practise asking a friend.
Say "Come and play" to a child who is alone.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to ask "Can I play?" and wait for the answer. Children: Children watch and listen.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "If a friend says yes, play. If not, try another friend." Children: Children nod and smile.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children practise asking a friend. Children: Child asks a friend.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Come and play" to a child who is alone. Children: Child invites a friend.

practical.title: Can I play?
steps: Invite a child who is alone.
practical.safety: Supervise the practice and keep it gentle so no child feels rejected. Pair shy children with a kind partner.

differentiation.support: Ask with the child and wait together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a friend who is alone and invite them.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you say to join?
What do you do for a lonely friend?

lessons.homeConnection: Practise asking to join a game at the park.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "practise asking to join a game" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Friends play together
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will play a cooperative game with friends.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name family members and show love in simple ways.
lessons.starter: Show the cloth and say "We hold the cloth together and make it go up and down."
teacherActivities: Show how to hold the cloth edge and lift it together.
Lift up and down while singing.
Roll the ball on the cloth.
learnerActivities: Children watch the ball and help.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to hold the cloth edge and lift it together. Children: Children hold the cloth.
Step 2. Teacher: Lift up and down while singing. Children: Children lift together.
Step 3. Teacher: Roll the ball on the cloth. Children: Children watch the ball and help.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We played together." Children: Children say we did it.

practical.title: Cloth game
practical.safety: Use a soft light cloth and a very soft ball and stand away from furniture. Keep the group small.

differentiation.support: Hold the cloth beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count up and down.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Plays a group game with friends
lessons.homeConnection: Play a group game with the family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play a cooperative game with friends" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Week 2 friends check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child plays with and behaves toward friends.
successCriteria: Says one thing a good friend does
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name family members and show love in simple ways.
lessons.starter: Sing the friendship song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: play, good friend and join a game.
At each station watch how the child plays and speaks.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: play, good friend and join a game. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child plays and speaks. Children: Child plays with a friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Friendship stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely and keep play gentle. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to welcome a quiet friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: plays with a friend; says what a good friend does; asks to join a game; includes others.

questions.question: What does a good friend do?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 2
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.

What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
